text.p: Severe flooding is ongoing in the US North Plains across many river systems. Cool temperatures for one more day keep snowmelt slow. After that, warmer weather will develop, quickening snowmelt, and may lead to even more severe flooding. Also, flooding conditions are expected to develop in Manitoba, Canada, the next several days as temperatures warm and a heavy snowpack melts.

A typhoon warning is up for the islands of Guam, Rota, Tinian and Saipan in the west Pacific. Typhoon Isa, with 115 mph winds, is near 11.1n/145.5e or about 175 miles south-southeast of Guam. Isa is expected to move to within 50 miles of Guam during the next 12 hours. Top winds increase to about 130 mph during the next 12-24 hours. This system is an extreme risk to shipping in the region from south of the Mariana islands through the islands and especially the region just west of the islands. In addition the islands can expect very strong winds and flooding rains as the system moves by. We expect damage to become high from this system.
There are no further emergency statements at this time.
